stories.title: AI Creditable Hours Programs Let Lawyers Experiment With Tech on Billable Time
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that a growing number of US firms give associates billable credit for time spent training on AI tools. Associates quoted in the piece say they welcome the chance to work hands-on with the technology. The article covers how these creditable hours programmes let lawyers experiment with AI on billable time.
stories.hook: More US firms let associates bill hours spent learning AI tools, Legal Tech Monitor reports

stories.title: Will Your Law Firm Build an AI Copy of You?
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that law firms including Davis Wright and Vorys are testing AI personas and digital twins of their lawyers. The article asks who will own such AI copies of attorneys and what questions firms should weigh. It is framed as commentary on the ownership of these tools rather than a report of a formal deployment.
stories.hook: Davis Wright and Vorys are testing AI personas of lawyers, raising questions over who owns them

stories.title: Future of Law Firm Tech Stacks Will Be Dominated by Centralized, Core Platforms
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor says leaders from Dechert and Willkie Farr & Gallagher discuss how law firm technology stacks may change, with centralised core platforms expected to dominate. The piece is based on the views of firm technology leaders rather than a survey or launch, and points to a shift in how firms organise their systems over the coming period.
stories.hook: Dechert and Willkie Farr leaders expect law firm tech stacks to centre on core platforms

stories.title: Adodo v Argos: Court of Appeal rules switching on a laptop does not break a "digital seal"
stories.ltme_summary: The Court of Appeal has held in Adodo v Argos that switching on a laptop bought online and activating its preloaded operating system does not cost the buyer the statutory right to cancel. Dr Ebenezer Adodo, who represented himself, won a second appeal and the court ordered Argos to refund the £379 price with interest. The judgment rejected Argos's argument that the Windows activation broke a digital seal.
stories.hook: Court of Appeal rules Argos must refund a laptop as switching it on broke no digital seal

The group includes 23 partners across New York, Washington and London, according to Reuters. The move follows the Weil partners' vote to wind down the firm, and other firms including Kirkland and Skadden are also taking Weil lawyers.

The column is opinion drawn from the author's own experience in Biglaw, and it does not cite survey data in the part provided.

What Could the EU’s Digital Fairness Act Mean for Your Business? // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.ltme_summary: Cooley's series on the EU Digital Fairness Act says the European Commission published its proposal on 11 November 2026. The proposal would replace 27 national regimes with a directly applicable regulation and allow the Commission to fine up to 6 per cent of worldwide annual turnover. It covers dark patterns, influencer marketing, personalisation, gaming and subscriptions, and now goes to Parliament and Council.
stories.hook: Cooley says the EU Digital Fairness Act proposal would let the Commission fine up to 6 per cent of global turnover

stories.title: Are You Compliant? UK CMA Unveils Guidance on New Subscription Rules // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.ltme_summary: Cooley reports that the UK government has published draft legislation and the CMA has issued draft guidance on subscription contract rules under the DMCC Act. Rules are now due to start in January 2027, brought forward from April 2027. The rules will apply to auto-renewing B2C contracts and set pre-contract information duties.
stories.hook: Cooley says UK subscription rules under the DMCC Act now start January 2027, not April 2027

stories.title: Treasury releases NPRM expanding Outbound Investment Security Program
stories.ltme_summary: Davis Polk says Treasury issued a proposed rule on 22 October 2026 implementing the COINS Act and expanding the Outbound Investment Security Program. The proposal adds sectors including AI and biotechnology and widens covered entities. Comments are due 7 December 2026, and the final rule is likely in Q1 2027.
stories.hook: Davis Polk says Treasury's outbound investment proposal widens AI and biotech coverage, comments due 7 December

stories.title: USPTO Returns Merits-Based Institution Decisions to PTAB, Clarifies Institution Standards | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: Morrison Foerster reports that USPTO Director John Squires issued a memorandum on 10 November 2026 returning merits-based institution decisions for IPR and PGR to PTAB three-judge panels, effective 16 November 2026. The Director keeps gatekeeping on non-merits issues and sets five guidelines for panels.
stories.hook: MoFo says USPTO returns merits-based IPR institution decisions to PTAB panels from 16 November 2026

stories.title: OCC Issues Supervisory Framework for Bank Use of Super Intelligence | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: Morrison Foerster reports that the OCC issued a supervisory framework on 4 November 2026 for examiners assessing banks' use of AI, which it terms super intelligence. The framework has six pillars and says it does not set new enforceable standards. It covers human oversight, risk tiering and vendor management.
stories.hook: MoFo says the OCC's AI supervisory framework sets no new enforceable standards for banks
entities: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

stories.title: MoFo Prepares Future Attys With New AI Summer Program | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: Morrison Foerster says it is launching a 1L Summer Innovation Associate role for summer 2027, recruiting two first-year law students. Summer associates will work with the firm's innovation team on AI tools and workflows for practice groups. Recruiting and innovation directors discussed the programme in a Law360 article.
stories.hook: Morrison Foerster will recruit two first-year students for an AI-focused summer associate role for 2027

The firm says the new conditions take effect on 1 April 2027, and that the consultation closes on 23 November 2026. Its draft reply on condition E11 criticises an example about governing body members and cites the University of Sussex ruling and the 2026 CUC Governance Code.
stories.hook: Shakespeare Martineau urges the OfS to drop a guidance example on governing body criticism before 23 November

Stat(s) Of The Week: An Uneasy Relationship
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports on Bloomberg Law's AI in Practice survey of attorneys. Half of respondents say they trust AI tools enough for complex tasks, and 92 per cent say they verify AI citations and quotations. A third of associates and 16 per cent of partners fear losing their jobs to AI. The survey was reported as a new Bloomberg Law report.
stories.hook: Bloomberg Law survey finds 92 per cent of attorneys verify every AI citation, while many fear for their jobs

stories.title: AI In Our Courts: Useful Or A Magic 8 Ball?
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law commentary contrasts a Texas federal judge's criticism of lawyers accused of using AI with a Eastern District of Kentucky ruling. In the Kentucky case, a detective allegedly used AI facial recognition alone to identify a man who was later shown to be elsewhere. The judge denied the officer's motion to dismiss, the author says. The piece argues courts should weigh how AI is used rather than condemn its use outright.
stories.hook: Above the Law contrasts a Kentucky court's handling of an AI facial recognition arrest with a Texas judge's attack on AI-drafted briefs
entities: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky

stories.title: Law Practice Management Win For Actionstep
stories.ltme_summary: Actionstep, a cloud practice management provider for midsize US law firms, says it won the Overall Practice Management Solution Provider of the Year category at the 2026 LegalTech Breakthrough Awards. The company says it serves more than 5,000 firms across North America, the UK, Australia and New Zealand. It highlights embedded AI time capture, which it says has helped firms recover 25 to 50 extra billable hours per lawyer per year.
stories.hook: Actionstep says its practice management platform won a 2026 LegalTech Breakthrough Award

AI for Lawyers: How to Govern AI After Deployment
stories.ltme_summary: Axiom publishes a summary of its on-demand CLE on governing AI after deployment. Speakers Axiom Legal Engineer David O'Hara and Draftpilot CEO Daniel van Binsbergen argue legal departments remain accountable for AI output after scale-up. The piece sets out a four-part governance framework and maps ABA Model Rules, including Rule 3.3 on verifying AI-generated citations.
stories.hook: Axiom and Draftpilot argue legal teams keep duty for AI output once tools move beyond pilot

stories.title: The Celeste advantage: The harness that empowers your agents to be the best they can be
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp describes Celeste, its Firm AI platform, as an operating layer for professional firms. The vendor argues that an agent harness, the runtime layer wrapping a large language model, can cut cost per answer and raise efficiency by encoding a firm's workflows. It names five harness components, including ReAct, DeepAgent and long-lived memory. The post cites Gartner's prediction that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled in 2027, and says only one in five firms have adequate infrastructure.
stories.hook: Intapp says its Celeste harness cuts agent costs by encoding each firm's workflows into the runtime layer

stories.title: Your law firm AI business case is a hypothesis. Keep testing it.
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp argues in a vendor post that law firms should treat AI business cases as hypotheses to test before and after go-live. It cites a 2026 Blickstein Group survey finding 66 per cent of law firm COOs do not formally document AI efficiency gains. The post says time capture and billing accuracy are central to measuring AI return, and promotes its Celeste Time product.
stories.hook: Intapp says law firms should treat AI business cases as hypotheses and test them against billing data

stories.title: Intapp board member Ralph Baxter receives The American Lawyer Lifetime Achievement Award
The Billable Hour Isn’t Dead. AI Might Be Reviving It.
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon's Director of Legal Spend and Analytics, Rhett Lemmel, argues in a Law.com interview, summarised by Integreon, that AI could revive the billable hour. He says firms have an incentive to lock in alternative fee arrangements before AI lowers their costs, while corporate clients will resist fixed fees until efficiency gains appear. The piece urges general counsel to focus on volume, staffing and scope in billing guidelines rather than rate alone.
stories.hook: Integreon argues AI gives law firms a reason to lock in fixed fees before their delivery costs fall

stories.title: The Most Revealing Performance Report in Your Immigration Practice Is Sitting in Your Inbox
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon's immigration practice article, dated 4 November 2026, argues that delays in immigration cases often arise inside a firm's own workflows, such as missing translations, unassigned tasks and unmonitored deadlines. It recommends stage-based timelines, clear ownership and visible progress tracking. The piece is part of Integreon's marketing on practice management for immigration firms.
stories.hook: Integreon says immigration firms should track internal case delays, not just client chasers
